items.title: A novel approach to employee well-being: Exploring proactive strategies for psychological needs satisfaction in daily life
items.abstract: Employee well-being is a critical aspect of individual fulfillment and organizational success. This is particularly true in today's landscape of work, characterized by increasing digitalization, flexibility, and a strong focus on performance. While these trends, further accelerated by the COVID-19 crisis, offer employees greater autonomy and growth opportunities, they also impose higher demands on self-management and proactive balance between work and nonwork life. Consequently, there is a need to equip employees with effective strategies to successfully navigate their work and nonwork situations so that they feel and perform well in both life domains. My research project investigates needs-based crafting as an innovative approach within occupational health psychology to enhance employee well-being and performance across both life domains. Traditional job design theories viewed employees as passive recipients of their work conditions. This perspective changed with the introduction of job crafting – a bottom-up approach, where employees proactively shape their jobs to align with their skills, needs and preferences. The rich empirical evidence accumulated thus far shows that job crafting is beneficial for employee well-being and motivation. However, existing job crafting models focus predominantly on proactive changes in pre-defined external stimuli and present challenges in their applicability outside the workplace. Addressing this, the needs-based model of crafting, rooted in psychological needs theory, proposes that employees craft their work and nonwork domains to fulfill six core psychological needs referred to as DRAMMA needs: detachment, relaxation, autonomy, mastery, meaning, and affiliation. This approach puts in center employee intrinsic motivation for crafting and thus can capture a wide range of crafting strategies relevant across different contexts in work and nonwork domains. Recently, quantitative scales have been developed to measure needs-based crafting, showing benefits for various aspects of well-being. Yet, a knowledge gap remains regarding the specific crafting strategies employees use in different work and nonwork contexts. My research project aims to fill this gap using ecological momentary assessment and natural language processing to collect real-time qualitative and quantitative data on employee crafting strategies. This innovative approach moves beyond the existing quantitatively focused crafting research to open the black box and provide insights into specific crafting strategies employees use to satisfy their DRAMMA needs across work and nonwork contexts. In addition, it will address the gap in the existing literature on the influences of individual and contextual factors on employee crafting strategies. Finally, the project will generate unique evidence about crafting strategies used by different profiles of employees based on their well-being outcomes. The findings of the project will contribute to the development of recommendations that will serve as an inspiration for employees to develop their own crafting strategies and as a basis for the development of crafting interventions aimed at promoting employee well-being and productivity. Overall, my project offers an innovative perspective on crafting research that will advance the theory and practice in the field of occupational health psychology.

items.title: A Scoping Review on the Management of Back Pain in Agricultural Workers
items.abstract: Objective: This scoping review aims to understand the extent and type of evidence for the effectiveness of self-management and participatory ergonomics strategies in agricultural working populations. Introduction: Low back pain is the most common musculoskeletal disorder in agricultural workers. While there is evidence supporting the prevalence of low back pain, there is a need to establish the current evidence for self-management and ergonomic interventions. Inclusion criteria: Studies focusing on workers in agriculture, including aquaculture, nursery, landscape, and other physically demanding outdoor occupations at risk for chronic back pain will be included. Of interest are self-management and participatory ergonomic prevention or intervention strategies, while surgical or pharmacological intervention studies will be excluded. Methods: The literature search will be carried out by a health science librarian using 15 bibliographic databases encompassing health, business, and agricultural topic areas. There will be no study type or publication date limits, but the search will be limited to English and Spanish language only. Following the search, all identified citations will be collated and uploaded into Covidence and duplicates automatically removed. Title/abstract and full text screening will occur with two independent reviewers, with a third reviewer resolving discrepancies. Data will be extracted by two independent reviewers using the final data extraction tool developed by the reviewers, with a third reviewer for consensus where needed.

items.title: Affiliate Motivation Theory
items.abstract: Rachmad, Yoesoep Edhie. 2023. Affiliate Motivation Theory. Lahore Minar Kitab Ishaat, Khaas Edition 2023. https://doi.org/10.17605/osf.io/pdgsk The Affiliate Motivation Theory, conceptualized by Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad and detailed in his 2023 publication "Lahore Minar Kitab Ishaat, Khaas Edition," delves into the factors that motivate individuals to participate in affiliate marketing programs. Since beginning his research in 2016, Rachmad has explored how various motivational aspects influence affiliates' engagement and success, fundamentally shaping the dynamics of affiliate networks and marketing strategies. This theory originates from the need to understand the driving forces behind the decision of individuals to become affiliates — that is, to promote products or services on behalf of a company and earn commissions from sales or leads generated. With the growing prevalence of affiliate marketing as a major digital marketing strategy, understanding what motivates affiliates becomes crucial for optimizing program effectiveness and affiliate satisfaction. The Affiliate Motivation Theory posits that motivation in affiliate marketing can be broadly categorized into intrinsic and extrinsic factors. Intrinsic motivation includes personal satisfaction, enjoyment of the marketing activity, and a passion for the product or niche itself. Extrinsic motivation encompasses financial incentives, recognition, and the social benefits of being part of an affiliate community. Rachmad concludes that a successful affiliate program must carefully balance these motivational factors to attract and retain productive affiliates. He suggests that while financial incentives are critical, providing additional value through training, support, and community-building can enhance affiliates' intrinsic motivation, leading to higher dedication and long-term engagement. He recommends that companies running affiliate programs should invest in understanding the specific needs and preferences of their affiliates, customize communications and rewards to meet these preferences, and continuously innovate their offerings to keep the affiliate engagement high. Rachmad also emphasizes the importance of transparency and trust in maintaining a healthy affiliate relationship, suggesting that clear communication about policies, payments, and performance metrics is essential. Overall, the Affiliate Motivation Theory offers a comprehensive look at the multifaceted motivations driving affiliate marketers. It provides valuable insights for companies looking to leverage affiliate marketing effectively, advocating for strategies that not only focus on competitive financial compensation but also foster a supportive and engaging affiliate environment. the author earned the title of Doctor of Humanity, hold a Ph.D. in Information Technology and a DBA in General Management. Since 2016, the author has been teaching at international universities in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and the USA. In 1999, the author founded the Education Training Centre (ETC), an organization dedicated to providing educational services and social support for the underprivileged. This organization offers shelter homes for children in need of a safe place to live and drop-in schools for those who need to continue their education. The ETC is also involved in research aimed at advancing science, which led to the author earning the title of Professor and joining the WPF. Additionally, the author is actively involved in global social development programs through the United Nations. They are a member of the UN Global Compact (id-137635), the UN Global Market (id-709131), and the UN ECOSOC (id-677556). The author has served as a reviewer for several international journals and book chapters, and has written numerous books and articles on a wide range of topics including Philosophy, Economics, Management, Arts and Culture, Anthropology, Law, Psychology, Education, Sociology, Health, Technology, Tourism, and Communication.

items.title: AMORi - Sensomotor Study
items.abstract: Energy-efficient driving (ecodriving) in electric vehicles (EVs) plays a crucial role in enhancing overall mobility sustainability and in improving drivers’ competencies while interacting with limited range resources, thus, their user experience. Ecodriving can be difficult due to volatile and bidirectional energy flows, hence, requires ecodriving knowledge and energy-related situation awareness (we refer to as Energy Dynamics Awareness, EDA). Ecodriving displays may facilitate more efficient driving by either providing energy-relevant information (e.g., instantaneous consumption displays) or action-oriented recommendations (e.g., instantaneous optimal speed signals). The objective of the present research is to observe and compare the effect of prototypes of these two ecodriving display types in comparison to a control group without display. Using the EcoSimLab EV driving simulator, participants have to drive different driving scenarios with the instruction to achieve low average energy consumption. We measure ecodriving perfomance (e.g., average consumption) and variables related to user experience in action regulation (e.g., EDA) to estimate the supporting effect of both displays. The driving scenarios are ordered according to their situation complexity to estimate interaction effects of driving task demands.

items.title: An optical daytime astronomy pathfinder for the Huntsman Telescope
items.abstract: Abstract Observing stars and satellites in optical wavelengths during the day (optical daytime astronomy) has begun a resurgence of interest. The recent dramatic dimming event of Betelgeuse has spurred interest in continuous monitoring of the brightest variable stars, even when an object is only visible during the day due to their proximity to the Sun. In addition, an exponential increase in the number of satellites being launched into low Earth orbit in recent years has driven an interest in optical daytime astronomy for the detection and monitoring of satellites in space situational awareness (SSA) networks. In this paper we explore the use of the Huntsman Telescope as an optical daytime astronomy facility, by conducting an exploratory survey using a pathfinder instrument. We find that an absolute photometric accuracy between 1–10% can be achieved during the day, with a detection limit of V band 4.6 mag at midday in sloan $g,$ and $r,$ wavelengths. In addition, we characterise the daytime sky brightness, colour, and observing conditions in order to achieve the most reliable and highest signal-to-noise observations within the limitations of the bright sky background. We undertake a 7-month survey of the brightness of Betelgeuse during the day and demonstrate that our results are in agreement with measurements from other observatories. Finally we present our preliminary results that demonstrate obtaining absolute photometric measurements of the International Space Station during the day.

items.title: Are there indications of publication bias in occupational health research? An examination of the literature and suggestions for future improvements
items.abstract: While replicability of findings is a cornerstones of empirical research, in various fields adjacent to occupational health, research has shown to be insufficiently reproducible. A discussion on the topic of replicability and questionable research practices is, as far as we are aware, lacking in the field of occupational health. In the current study we therefore aim to evaluate indications of publication bias in the occupational health research literature. Ideally this would be done by large scale replications, which require considerable resources. A less resource-intense alternative is to screen a published body of evidence for indicators of publication bias, which might indicate low replicability and insufficient robustness of the evidence base. In the current protocol, we propose the methods of conducting a z-curve analysis by applying an existing text mining algorithm to articles published in the ten highest ranked occupational health journals. This algorithm can ‘scrape’ abstracts of all publications and extract relevant statistics from it (i.e., p-values and/or confidence intervals of various effect measures). Our pilot data analysis, using data from the years 2010 and 2020 only, was successful as a result of which we expect to be able to carry out the main analyses on the full dataset.

items.title: Bidirectional Progressive Neural Networks With Episodic Return Progress for Emergent Task Sequencing and Robotic Skill Transfer
items.abstract: Human brain and behavior provide a rich venue that can inspire novel control and learning methods for robotics. In an attempt to exemplify such a development by inspiring how humans acquire knowledge and transfer skills among tasks, we introduce a novel multi-task reinforcement learning framework named Episodic Return Progress with Bidirectional Progressive Neural Networks (ERP-BPNN). The proposed ERP-BPNN model 1) learns in a human-like interleaved manner by 2) autonomous task switching based on a novel intrinsic motivation signal and, in contrast to existing methods, 3) allows bidirectional skill transfer among tasks. ERP-BPNN is a general architecture applicable to several multi-task learning settings; in this paper, we present the details of its neural architecture and show its ability to enable effective learning and skill transfer among morphologically different robots in a reaching task. The developed Bidirectional Progressive Neural Network (BPNN) architecture enables bidirectional skill transfer without requiring incremental training and seamlessly integrates with online task arbitration. The task arbitration mechanism developed is based on soft Episodic Return progress (ERP), a novel intrinsic motivation (IM) signal. To evaluate our method, we use quantifiable robotics metrics such as ‘expected distance to goal’ and ‘path straightness’ in addition to the usual reward-based measure of episodic return common in reinforcement learning. With simulation experiments, we show that ERP-BPNN achieves faster cumulative convergence and improves performance in all metrics considered among morphologically different robots compared to the baselines. Overall, our method provides a human-inspired and efficient multi-task reinforcement learning approach with interleaved learning, making it highly suitable for lifelong learning applications.

items.title: Career Guidance and Counseling in Ukrainian Educational System: Pre-Institutional Phase
items.abstract: Theoretical Background: In the modern world career guidance and counseling is an important tool for an effective functioning of social system, as well as for ensuring the subjective well-being of individual members of society. Due to this fact the scientific interest towards career counseling constantly increases (Garriott et al., 2017). The attention mostly focuses on state policies in the field of career counseling (Kettunen et al., 2016), personality-oriented and value-oriented approaches in counseling (Niles & Guttierez, 2019), possibilities of using computer-assisted career guidance systems (Osborn, 2021), etc. Among other areas of practical implementation, сareer guidance and counseling in the education system is of particular importance. School age, especially adolescence, marks a pivotal stage when individuals face their first career decisions (Sharma, 2022), often without the life experience necessary to fully evaluate their strengths and potential (Marciniak et al., 2020). This period, defined by the development of personal identity, adds complexity to the process of choosing a career (Branje, 2022). External influences, such as parental expectations and peer pressure, can push adolescents toward professions that may not align with their true passions and aspirations (Kazi & Akhlaq, 2017). Additionally, the rapid pace of technological advancement and the emergence of new professions create uncertainty, making it challenging to anticipate future career demands and opportunities (Bankins et al., 2024). However, access to comprehensive career counselling and the cultivation of intrinsic motivation – rooted in personal interests and values – are essential for fostering a well-informed and successful career trajectory as well as for subjective well-being. An important factor in career decision-making activities is career motivation (Guay, 2005; Priyashantha et al., 2022). Within the framework of our study, the theory of Autonomous Career Motivation (ACM) should be considered. ACM is a recently developed construct based on Self-Determination Theory (Ryan & Deci, 2000) and related to personal motivation for professional development and career building (Sverko & Babarovic, 2024). Researching the features of autonomous career motivation of Ukrainian high school seniors and its relationship with career counseling services received will allow us to more deeply analyze the studied problem. In Ukrainian system of secondary education, the duties of a career counselor are not yet institutionalized. Furthermore, there are no training programs for specialists who would provide professional career guidance and counseling, working in the education system. It should be mentioned that the first steps in this direction are currently being taken. In particular, at the Borys Grinchenko Kyiv Metropolitan University, with the support of the National Education Agency of Finland, educational programs for the training of career counselors are being developed (CARE, 2023). But the lack of institutionalization does not mean that Ukrainian high school seniors are deprived of the opportunity to receive assistance in choosing a future career. Currently, a wide range of career counseling functions are shared between school psychologists and high school teachers. Although this approach can only partially cover the functionality of trained career counselors, before introducing specialised career guidance and counseling into Ukrainian schools, it is important to understand what is already being implemented in this field and how it actually works.
